title: Flat resolutions under ringed slice extension
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small in the fixed module universe, with $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $V\in\mathcal C$. Use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/V,R|_V)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], total cochain tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $e_!$ be sheafification of the direct-sum extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $P$ is a possibly unbounded K-flat complex of $R|_V$-modules, then $e_!P$ is K-flat over $R$. If every term of $P$ is flat (tensoring with that term is exact), every term of $e_!P$ is flat. A termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ remains one after applying $e_!$. For strict inverse sequences, these assertions apply objectwise to complexes of towers [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; in particular an objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement remains an objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement, with its original strict transition maps. No boundedness, quasi-compactness or regularity assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Write $j^*$ for restriction to $\mathcal C/V$ and $e_!$ for the functor in the statement. The exact-adjunction lemma identifies precisely this sheafified direct-sum extension and says that both functors are exact. For either $F=e_!$ or $F=j^*$, apply exactness to $0\to Z^iX\to X^i\to B^{i+1}X\to0$ and $0\to B^iX\to Z^iX\to H^iX\to0$. The first identifies the cycles and boundaries after applying $F$; the second gives $H^i(FX)\cong F(H^iX)$, naturally in chain maps. In particular either functor sends acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. This is a degreewise calculation for every integer $i$, without boundedness.

proof.text: Let $A$ be an acyclic complex of $R$-modules. By step 1, $j^*A$ is acyclic. The unbounded total-tensor comparison gives $\operatorname{Tot}(e_!P\otimes_R A)\cong e_!\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{R|_V}j^*A)$. The inner complex is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$, and its extension is acyclic by step 1. Thus $e_!P$ is K-flat. Here the order of the two tensor factors is immaterial: the signed swap on the $(p,q)$ summand is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$; substitution in $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ verifies it is a chain isomorphism, inverse to the same signed swap. The cited comparison is for direct-sum totalization and all unbounded complexes, so no convergence or product-totalization assertion is needed.

proof.text: Fix a flat term $M=P^i$ and a short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ of $R$-modules. Exact restriction gives a short exact sequence of the $j^*F_a$. Flatness of $M$ gives an exact sequence after tensoring these three modules with $M$, and exactness of $e_!$ preserves it. The natural sheaf projection isomorphisms $e_!(M\otimes j^*F_a)\cong e_!M\otimes F_a$ identify its arrows with the tensor maps induced by $F_1\to F_2\to F_3$. Hence tensoring with $e_!M$ is exact, which is precisely flatness. Apply this separately for each $i$.

proof.text: Let $q:P\to C$ be the given termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism, where surjective means epimorphic in the category of module sheaves. For each $i$, the short exact sequence $0\to\ker(q^i)\to P^i\to C^i\to0$ stays exact under $e_!$, so $e_!q^i$ is epimorphic. The natural homology identification of step 1 identifies $H^i(e_!q)$ with $e_!H^i(q)$, an isomorphism because a functor sends an inverse pair to an inverse pair. Thus $e_!q$ is a quasi-isomorphism as well as termwise surjective. Combining with steps 2 and 3 proves preservation of a flat-term K-flat replacement.

proof.text: For a strict inverse sequence of complexes with transition maps $t_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$, apply $e_!$ to every term, differential, transition and resolution map. The chain-map and tower commutation equations remain equations because $e_!$ preserves composition. Steps 2 and 3 apply to each $P_n$ and step 4 to each resolution map. Kernels and cokernels in the tower category are levelwise by the cited tower lemma, so epimorphisms and cohomology isomorphisms of these tower complexes are detected at every level. The resulting transitions are exactly $e_!(t_n)$, without replacing the strict system or choosing levelwise comparison maps. This proves precisely the objectwise assertion in the statement.
